summary: CaF2, SrF2, and ZnF2 thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at temperatures between 260 and 400°C. The study investigates the growth properties, crystallinity, stoichiometry, and optical and electrical characteristics of these films. The films were grown on soda-lime glass substrates coated with Al2O3. The growth rate varied depending on the material and temperature, and the films showed good crystallinity. The study also explores the use of these films in multilayer structures for optical applications.
evidence: CaF2, SrF2, and ZnF2 thin films have been deposited on glass substrates for the first time using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at temperatures between 260 and 400°C. The source materials used are alkaline earth β-diketonates, zinc acetate dihydrate, and hydrogen fluoride in nitrogen atmosphere. The growth rate of films varies from 20 to 90 Å/cycle depending on materials and temperature. The crystallinity, orientation, stoichiometry, atomic density, optical and electrical properties together with growth properties of the films have been characterized.
